- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3 periods.  
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 2+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast toward that average.  
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3 days, model lags; forecast should rise 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
